item.description: ‘There are generations who came before us and left these natural resources. We should do the same and leave wealth’

item.title: ZRP Says Officers Sent To Tendai Biti’s Offices To Maintain Order
item.description: The Zimbabwe Republic Police (ZRP) has confirmed deploying officers to Tendai Biti’s offices from the morning of Thursday, 5 March 2026.

item.title: TIMB Says Tobacco Prices Stabilising After Shock $0.35/kg Sales
item.description: The Tobacco Industry and Marketing Board (TIMB) has moved to reassure farmers that tobacco prices are beginning to stabilise, a day after some bales were sold for as little as US$0.35 per kilogramme on Wednesday, shortly after the official opening of the 2026 tobacco marketing season.

item.title: High Court sets aside ruling in mining dispute involving Zanu-PF MP
item.description: The Bulawayo High Court has set aside a determination made by the Midlands Provincial Mining Director (PMD) in a dispute over mining claim boundaries, ruling that the official improperly delegated his powers to subordinates before deciding the matter.

item.title: Bulawayo council pushes online billing as unpaid rates soar
item.description: Residents in Bulawayo have been urged to sign up for an online billing system as the city council moves to improve revenue collection and reduce the use of paper bills.

item.title: MPs raise concern over low visibility of Women’s Microfinance Bank
item.description: More than 49 000 women and small-scale entrepreneurs across Zimbabwe have benefited from loans disbursed by the Zimbabwe Women’s Microfinance Bank (ZWMB) since its establishment in 2018, according to a parliamentary report that examined the institution’s performance.

item.title: Byo councillors sign anti-corruption pledge after earlier resistance
item.description: Councillors in Bulawayo have signed an integrity pledge aimed at strengthening transparency and accountability in local governance.

item.title: Solar power in rural Zimbabwe hasn’t reduced women’s unpaid work: can policy do better?
item.description: Some women in Zimbabwe are being left behind in the move to green energy because they can’t afford solar systems that can power electric stoves.
